# AI use statement {.unnumbered}

<!-- Draft for the authors to confirm or correct before submission. -->

We used an AI coding agent (Claude) extensively in this work. It wrote and ran
experiment code, managed jobs on a remote workstation, aggregated results, generated
the figures from the committed result files, and drafted and edited manuscript text.
Research questions, experimental designs and decision rules were discussed with the
agent. After the initial couplet split, every design and decision rule was committed
to version control before the corresponding result was computed. The authors reviewed the code, the committed
results and every claim in the manuscript. Numbers in the text were checked against
the machine-readable result files, and citations were checked against their sources, except two added at the end
(\texttt{goyal2024pause}, \texttt{hao2024coconut}), which the authors should confirm. We take responsibility for the final content of this work, including
text, claims and artifacts produced with the aid of generative AI.

# Ethics statement {.unnumbered}

This work studies how openly released language models use information they have
not written. Its aim is to support the monitoring of such models. It involves no
human subjects, personal data or harmful content. The hidden-choice task elicits
harmless secret choices (fruits, animals). The results locate where content that the
text does not reveal is stored, which is information useful to monitors. We do not
see a plausible route by which it helps a model conceal content. The limitations
section states where the findings may not transfer, notably to long reasoning with
thinking enabled and to models trained to conceal.

# Reproducibility statement {.unnumbered}

All experiments use publicly released checkpoints (Appendix @sec-app-materials) and
public prompts, either released by @hanna2026latent and @ma2026plan or generated
with fixed seeds. For every experiment, the anonymized repository contains the code,
the design and decision rule as committed before the first result, the per-item
result rows and summaries with bootstrap intervals, and the scripts that generate
every figure and table from those files. The log of committed decision rules (Appendix
@sec-app-prereg) lists each frozen design, its decision rule, the outcome and all
dated deviations. Interventions, clamping and batching were checked against
unbatched reference implementations. Compute is described in Appendix
@sec-app-compute.
